title: Arbitrarily precise arrival time measurements in quantum mechanics
summary: The quantum Zeno effect is often regarded as an obstruction to precise arrival time measurements in quantum mechanics. Here, an arbitrarily precise arrival time measurement procedure is constructed using a localized detection process and a suitably chosen boundary condition. The arrival time of an incoming particle is recorded in the position of a clock particle that is emitted by the apparatus upon detection.
